sections.skill: Build a service estimate from time, rate, materials and contingency

questions.prompt: Which time should be included in an estimate?

choices.text: Only the minutes spent doing the main task itself
Only travel, since the work is the easy part
Only the time the customer can see you working
All of it: setup, travel, cleanup, messages and the work

questions.correct_answer: All of it: setup, travel, cleanup, messages and the work
questions.intro: To estimate a service job, list every part of the work and estimate time for each, including setup, travel, cleanup and communication. Multiply total hours by your hourly rate, add materials, and add a small CONTINGENCY for surprises (for example 10 percent). Example: 6 hours at 45 dollars = 270, plus 60 dollars of materials = 330, plus 10 percent = 363 dollars. Afterward, compare actual time with the estimate and adjust future estimates.

questions.intro: An estimate combines multiplication and addition: (hours x rate) + materials, then add the contingency percent. Example: 3 hours at 50 = 150; + 30 materials = 180; x 1.10 = 198. Do the steps in order. A common mistake is applying the percent before adding materials, which leaves the materials uncovered by the buffer. Checking each step on paper avoids that slip.
